supporting_observations.claim: The alerted PowerShell activity is visible at 13:42:01 UTC on WS-ICHEN-01. It ran as NWD\sam.okafor, and its command line invoked the exact \FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1 path specified in the organization's IT practices.
Shortly before PowerShell started, WS-ICHEN-01 received a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01. The logon ID matches the one on the PowerShell process.

The activity aligns with the scheduled business-hours patching practice: PowerShell connected through the proxy to download.windowsupdate.com, then launched wusa to install a Windows update package; both child activity and PowerShell termination are logged.

The process-creation, network, child-process, and process-termination records provide positive detail about what the alerted PowerShell execution did during the window, rather than relying only on a lack of suspicious events.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show the PowerShell command line and observed execution chain, but do not include the contents or hash of Apply-Updates.ps1.
The logs establish that PowerShell ran, but do not establish whether ivy.chen saw an interactive window or precisely how long it was visible.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not independently verify the integrity or contents of the script at the referenced network path.
The evidence does not establish the precise appearance or duration of the reported PowerShell window.
unrelated_findings: A Firefox process opened a Citrix StoreWeb URL on customer.cloud.com, a service not identified in the approved-services context; review separately if appropriate. Records: T044-00163, T044-00167, T044-00171, T044-00172.
Cisco Spark/Webex was launched with an app.slack.com URL, also not identified in the approved-services context; review separately. Records: T044-00168, T044-00170.
